mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate earnings, which in turn depresses S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.5% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals weakening labor market conditions, which typically precedes a downturn in consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE rose by more than 0.5% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals a weakening demand environment, which leads to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances where RSAFS declined for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a month signals a strengthening supply side, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances where INDPRO increased by more than 2% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4.5% and the CPI (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure combined with tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.3% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS was above 4.5% and CPIAUCSL increased by more than 0.3% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in a month signals a weakening labor market, which typically precedes a downturn in consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where PAYEMS decreased by more than 100,000 in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 10% in a month and real GDP (GDPC1) growth is below 2% in the previous quarter, it signals a weakening demand environment combined with a slowing economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST declines > 10% in 1 month and GDPC1 growth < 2% in previous quarter
regime_hint: economic slowdown with weak housing sector
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances where HOUST declined by more than 10% and GDPC1 growth was below 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over three consecutive months signals an easing monetary cycle, which typically leads to increased investment and consumer spending, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS declined for three consecutive months.
